question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
Yes. In August 2026, electricity prices were **13.2% higher than a year earlier**, against **4.0%** for all groups CPI. The gap is 9.2 percentage points.

The recent path:

| Period | Electricity (y/y) | All groups (y/y) |
|---|---|---|
| Jan 2026 | 32.2% | 3.8% |
| Feb 2026 | 37.0% | 3.7% |
| Mar 2026 | 25.4% | 4.6% |
| Jun 2026 | 22.4% | 3.8% |
| Jul 2026 | 6.1% | 3.5% |
| Aug 2026 | 13.2% | 4.0% |

Electricity has been well ahead of overall inflation since mid-2025. Its annual rate peaked at 37.0% in February 2026 and has since slowed, though not steadily. The July 2026 drop to 6.1% and the rebound to 13.2% in August suggest the annual rate is sensitive to timing effects.

Those timing effects matter for reading the numbers. In 2024 electricity prices were sharply lower than a year earlier (down 35.6% in October 2024), and from July 2025 the annual rate swung sharply positive. Much of that swing reflects comparisons against a low or high base a year earlier, not just the underlying price trend. I haven't checked the cause of those 2024–25 movements against the source, so treat the explanation as likely rather than confirmed.
